name: Strait of Malacca
note: Carries roughly a quarter of the world's traded goods by sea.
description: The Strait of Malacca is the main street of Asian trade — an eight-hundred-kilometre funnel between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra joining the Indian Ocean to the Pacific rim. It is the shortest sea route between the Middle East's oil and East Asia's factories, and it narrows near Singapore to channels barely wider than the ships that use them. Whoever has held its shores has prospered by it: the sultans of Malacca, the Portuguese who took the city in 1511, the Dutch and British after them, and the port states of today, for whom the strait remains both artery and vulnerability.
